set.descent_text: The usual way down is the South Face rappel line: from the summit, rappel the bolted route in about four rope lengths to Pineapple Pass, where the stations are easy to find, then reverse the approach down the basin talus and the climbers' path to the Alpental lot. Unroped parties often downclimb the North Ridge instead; it is class 4 with a slabby section and real exposure, and it should be done dry because the slab ends in a long drop.
set.approach: From the Alpental lot, hike the Snow Lake Trail to the signed split onto the Source Lake Overlook trail, and take it. Past Source Lake the path crosses talus, then a cairned climbers' path leaves left and skirts beneath the cliffs into the basin below Bryant, Hemlock and The Tooth, with Pineapple Pass (about 5,280 ft) at the head of the basin. The North Ridge starts on the north side of the peak: from the basin drop about 100 ft and traverse northwest to reach the ridge crest.

review.notes: WTA report climbed the North Ridge and descended four South Face rappels, plus approach and Pineapple Pass elevation; MP area page for the Source Lake Overlook path; MP route page for 4th class, N side, unroped descent preference.

set.descent_text: Descend the couloir you climbed. From the summit block downclimb the short third-class step, then rappel from the tree anchor just below the summit into the head of the couloir; the steeper, narrower sections lower down are also handled by rappel or downclimbing, depending on how much snow is left. Late in the season the couloir fills with loose class 3-4 rock, which is hard to downclimb and sends rockfall onto anyone below, so it is best done while snow still covers it. Once out of the couloir, walk down the open slope and the snow-covered approach to the Blue Lake trailhead.

review.notes: Trip report on stevensong.com: summit block, tree-anchor rappels into the couloir, walk out. Mountaineers trip report snippet (page blocked to scripts) agrees on the tree rappel then more rappel past the narrow section; rappel count differs so none is stated. Late-season loose rock from a SummitPost snippet.

set.descent_text: Rather than reverse the exposed class 4 ledges of the north face, rappel the Northeast Ridge on a single rope, using the fixed slings along it, back to the camp on the Chopping Block ridge (about 6,400 ft). The way out from there is long and steep: work across Stump Hollow, a mix of snow, slab and heather, up to the Barrier crest, follow a faint path down the crest from timberline (about 5,600 ft) to a minor saddle near 3,600 ft, then drop steeply through brush and cliff bands to the log crossing of Terror Creek (about 2,000 ft). The Goodell Creek Trail is reached near 1,700 ft and leads to the trailhead; allow roughly 7 hours from camp.

review.notes: Trip report with NW Route, a rappel down the NE Ridge, and the day-5 exit via Stump Hollow, Barrier crest, Terror Creek and Goodell Creek with elevations and time. Single-rope and fixed slings are from the stored text and the NE Ridge sibling.
